issues.description: The problem text first instructs students to create a final Stock instance field initialized in the constructor (an instance field), but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and shared across all SealSaloon instances. This is internally contradictory and the solution implements stock as a static final field initialized at declaration. Students may implement an instance final stock in the constructor (as described earlier) and then be confused when the later requirement and the reference solution expect a static shared stock, causing compilation or behavioral mismatches with the provided tests and the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) require and show stock as a static shared field (e.g., declare private static final Stock stock and explain it is initialized once), or (B) require an instance final Stock assigned in the constructor and then make acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice instance methods (remove the note that stock/methods must be static). Update the UML and all textual instructions to match the chosen approach. Prefer option A if the intention is a shared stock (aligns with the current solution).

issues.description: The problem statement requires a modifiable List<Meal> attribute called orders, but the provided helper code (ArrayHelpers) and the reference solution use arrays (Meal[]) for orders. This mismatch between the specified type (List<Meal>) and the array-based template/solution can confuse students about which collection type to use and which utilities to call (List methods vs. ArrayHelpers).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and the template: either change the problem text to request a modifiable Meal[] orders (and mention ArrayHelpers usage), or update the template and solution to use List<Meal> (e.g., ArrayList<Meal>) and remove or adapt ArrayHelpers. Ensure the UML, textual description, and provided helper utilities consistently indicate the same collection type so students know which API to use.
